title: HPC with Enhanced User Separation
problem: User-modified HPC software is rarely built with security in mind, creating risks in shared systems. Systems require enforcement of separation across processes, filesystem access, network traffic, and accelerators to prevent interference between users.
motivation: Shared HPC systems must support diverse research workflows while maintaining strong isolation guarantees to prevent security breaches and resource interference between users.
method: MIT Lincoln Laboratory's Supercomputing Center deployed enforced separation techniques spanning process isolation, filesystem access controls, network traffic isolation, and accelerator constraints. These mechanisms collectively create the abstraction of a personal HPC system for each user within a shared infrastructure.
key_novelty: Holistic enforcement of user separation across processes, filesystem, network, and accelerators to achieve strong multi-tenant isolation in HPC systems.
contributions: Process isolation enforcement for HPC workloads
Filesystem access control and isolation techniques
